headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors via Haystack MCP and Dexter’s autonomous file/API workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are medium.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and broad network egress, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content through shared MCP or API channels. Dexter runs autonomous execution and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, making it plausible it will consume Haystack outputs as instructions. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so interaction risk is high.
conditions: IF Haystack is connected to an MCP server that relays untrusted content into Dexter's workflow
IF Dexter parses scratchpad or API-returned text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable MCP bridges between the agents for untrusted content
Prefix all inter-agent messages with machine-readable provenance tags
Require a human review step before Dexter acts on Haystack output
Restrict Dexter to read-only mode for any Haystack-fed inputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys, while Haystack can call REST/MCP endpoints and also has broad egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so leakage is not proven, but if either agent forwards the other's context to external services, sensitive data could leave the boundary.
conditions: IF Dexter sends financial or market data into external APIs
IF Haystack forwards shared context or retrieved documents to a third-party REST or MCP endpoint
mitigations: Remove sensitive fields from prompts before handoff
Use separate API credentials per agent
Block outbound requests except to approved endpoints
Log and review all inter-agent payloads for secrets
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while Haystack can use MCP servers and REST APIs. The profiles do not show a shared lock or shared mutable directory, so direct conflict is not certain, but overlapping networked actions and local writes can still race if orchestrated together.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or scratchpad
IF an orchestrator runs concurrent writes without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a simple lock file
Disable concurrent runs during shared-resource updates
Review for overlapping API side effects before execution
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG agent that can consume and re-emit retrieved content, and Dexter runs autonomously with broad egress. If Dexter's outputs become Haystack inputs without verification, Haystack may treat generated text as authoritative and propagate errors into downstream actions or reports. The profiles show no built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF Haystack uses Dexter output as retrieved evidence or final answer text
IF Dexter-generated claims are forwarded into downstream actions without validation
mitigations: Insert a verification step between Dexter and Haystack
Mark Dexter outputs as untrusted in Haystack prompts
Require citations from primary sources before action
Limit Haystack to summarization only for Dexter-fed content
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial data and market data and handles multiple API keys, while Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. The profiles do not show a residency or retention mismatch, but the presence of financial data on one side and telemetry-style data on the other creates a plausible compliance gap if the pair shares logs or exports across boundaries.
conditions: IF financial data is logged into Haystack telemetry or usage analytics
IF shared exports mix market data with anonymous usage statistics
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from logs and analytics
Separate retention policies by data class
Review data-processing notices for both agents
Disable telemetry on sensitive runs
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
